# Clean Architecture Overview

AniTrend v2 follows a **multi-layered Clean Architecture** approach (see [README.md#L6-L14](https://github.com/AniTrend/support-arch/blob/1d33ef7ec3f48d4ba2bdeca82b55a23f0de0e2cc/README.md#L6-L14)). The codebase is organized into distinct layers (and Gradle modules) for **domain**, **data**, and **presentation**, each with clear responsibilities: - **Domain layer** – Pure Kotlin logic: defines use cases (interactors), repository interfaces, and domain models (entities). It contains no Android framework code, making it easy to unit test. - **Data layer** – Implements the repository interfaces and handles data sources (network, database, cache). It includes API clients, database DAOs/entities, and mappers. Data layer produces `UiState` or `DataState` results (from the `support-arch` library) which encapsulate data flows and loading states for the UI (see [tag/repository/ITagRepository.kt#L22-L28](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/domain/src/main/kotlin/co/anitrend/domain/tag/repository/ITagRepository.kt#L22-L28)). - **Presentation layer** – Android UI and related logic. In AniTrend v2 this is split into **feature modules** (each representing a screen or flow) and some common UI modules. It contains Activities/Fragments or Composables, ViewModels, and UI-specific classes. This layer consumes the domain use cases and observes `UiState`/`DataState` outputs to update the UI.

This separation ensures that business logic (domain) is decoupled from UI and data details, following Clean Architecture principles (see [README.md#L6-L14](https://github.com/AniTrend/support-arch/blob/1d33ef7ec3f48d4ba2bdeca82b55a23f0de0e2cc/README.md#L6-L14)). The app logic is easier to maintain and test since each layer can evolve independently.

**Resource Management:** String resources follow a consistent naming convention across all modules using semantic prefixes (`label_`, `title_`, `placeholder_`, `action_`, etc.) combined with module context. This ensures maintainability and enables effective AI assistance in code generation and maintenance.

## Module Organization and Naming

The project is divided into many Gradle modules, categorized by layer and feature. Key module groups include: - **App modules** (`:app:` prefix) – The application entry point and container. For example, `:app:main` is the main application module, and there are submodules like `:app:core` (app-wide initialization, configurations) and `:app:navigation` (navigation graph handling) (see [buildSrc/module/Modules.kt#L40-L48](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/buildSrc/src/main/java/co/anitrend/buildSrc/module/Modules.kt#L40-L48)). The app module depends on all other feature, domain, data modules to assemble the app. - **Domain modules** (`:domain:` prefix) – Currently mainly `:domain` (common domain). It defines all use case classes (often named `*UseCase` or `*Interactor`) and repository interfaces (e.g. `ITagRepository`) for each domain concept. Domain models (entity classes) and business logic live here. There is typically a one-to-one mapping between a domain package (e.g. `co.anitrend.domain.tag`) and a corresponding data package for implementations. - **Data modules** (`:data:` prefix) – There are multiple data modules, each focusing on a specific concern or external source. For example: `:data:core` might hold core data utilities (like network API configuration), `:data:android` may have Android-specific data helpers (content providers, etc.), and others like `:data:tmdb`, `:data:trakt`, `:data:jikan`, `:data:imgur` implement integration with those external APIs. Each data module typically provides one or more repository implementations and data sources. A “common” data module (`:data` or `:data:common`) contains shared data models or logic used across others. All data modules rely on the **support-arch** library’s data components (e.g., `arch.data`, `arch.request`) for unified handling of requests and states. - **Android platform modules** (`:android:` prefix) – Provide Android-specific components that are shared across features (e.g., `:android:core` for base Android utilities, or `:android:deeplink` for navigation deep links). These contain things like context-aware utilities, resource providers, or Android service integrations that don’t fit in pure domain or data layers. - **Common feature logic modules** (`:common:` prefix) – Reusable UI logic or components for a specific domain. For example, `:common:media`, `:common:character`, etc., hold UI models, view components, or logic that multiple features might use. These modules help avoid duplication by sharing code between feature screens related to the same entity (like media or characters). - **Feature modules** (`:feature:` prefix) – Each feature module corresponds to a distinct screen or user-facing feature. These are typically Android UI modules (often using Jetpack Compose). For instance, `:feature:auth` (authentication UI), `:feature:media:discover` (media discovery screen), `:feature:settings` (settings screen), etc. Feature modules contain ViewModels, Composables/Fragments, and use cases specific to that feature. They depend on relevant domain and common modules. The list of feature modules is extensive (see [buildSrc/module/Modules.kt#L92-L100](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/buildSrc/src/main/java/co/anitrend/buildSrc/module/Modules.kt#L92-L100)), covering various app sections (from browsing media, profiles, to notifications and more). This modularization allows features to be developed and maintained in isolation. - **Task modules** (`:task:` prefix) – These modules encapsulate background work (often executed via WorkManager). For example, `:task:sync`, `:task:character`, `:task:notification`, etc., likely define `Worker` classes for background synchronization or updates related to those domains. They allow background tasks to be packaged separately from UI, and they depend on data/domain layers to perform their work. Each task module typically contains a WorkManager worker and any supporting logic for that background task. - **Support libraries** – In addition to the above, the project includes several in-house libraries (as separate Gradle modules or external dependencies via JitPack): - **support-arch** – Provides the foundational architecture components (UI, data, domain, etc.). This is used extensively in all layers (e.g., base classes for view models, states, data sources). - **support-query-builder** – Used for building queries (SQL or GraphQL) through annotations and DSL, providing type-safe query generation. - **support-markdown** – Utility for rendering markdown text in the app. - **Others:** There are also modules like `:material-multi-search` (a UI component for search), `:android-emojify` (handles emoji support), and `:retrofit-graphql` (Retrofit integration for GraphQL). These are discussed in the context below.

Each module’s **Gradle path and naming** is defined in a centralized place (`buildSrc/Modules.kt`), which enumerates all module IDs (see [buildSrc/module/Modules.kt#L40-L48](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/buildSrc/src/main/java/co/anitrend/buildSrc/module/Modules.kt#L40-L48), [buildSrc/module/Modules.kt#L92-L100](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/buildSrc/src/main/java/co/anitrend/buildSrc/module/Modules.kt#L92-L100)). This makes it easy to include module dependencies in a consistent way (e.g., using `project(Modules.Feature.Media.path)` in Gradle). When adding new modules, you should update this Modules registry so that build scripts and dependency injection include the new module.

## Communication Between Layers

Layers communicate via well-defined interfaces: - The UI (feature modules) talks to the domain layer by invoking use case classes. For example, a ViewModel in a feature module might call `TagUseCase.getMediaTags(param)` which is defined in `:domain` (see [tag/interactor/TagUseCase.kt#L23-L31](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/domain/src/main/kotlin/co/anitrend/domain/tag/interactor/TagUseCase.kt#L23-L31)). - Domain use cases internally rely on repository interfaces (e.g. `ITagRepository`) which are also in the domain layer (see [tag/repository/ITagRepository.kt#L22-L28](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/domain/src/main/kotlin/co/anitrend/domain/tag/repository/ITagRepository.kt#L22-L28)). The use case doesn’t know about the data layer; it just calls the repository interface. - The data layer provides concrete implementations of those domain repository interfaces (e.g. `TagRepository` implements `ITagRepository`) and is bound via dependency injection. The data layer can aggregate multiple sources (network, cache, etc.) to fulfill a repository request. In AniTrend, these repositories often return a **DataState** or **UiState** object containing a Flow of data and a Flow of loading status, rather than a raw value. This helps the UI to easily observe asynchronous data and loading/error states. - Data sources within the data layer perform the actual operations. For network calls, the app uses **Retrofit** (with a custom GraphQL converter). The responses come back in a `GraphQLResponse<*>` wrapper, which the data layer then maps to domain entities and caches in a Room database. For database, the app uses **Room** ORM with DAO interfaces. The data layer may also define **mappers** to convert network models to database entities and domain models. - **Koin** (a Kotlin dependency injection framework) is used to wire these layers together at runtime. Each module (especially data modules) provides a Koin module that tells how to construct its components (e.g., which implementation to use for a repository interface, how to provide a Retrofit API instance, etc.). At app startup, all these modules are loaded so that when a ViewModel requests a `TagUseCase` or a repository, Koin can provide the correct instance from the data layer.

For example, the **Tag feature** follows this pattern: - Domain `TagUseCase` (in `:domain`) defines `getMediaTags()` and depends on an `ITagRepository` (see [tag/interactor/TagUseCase.kt#L19-L27](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/domain/src/main/kotlin/co/anitrend/domain/tag/interactor/TagUseCase.kt#L19-L27), [tag/repository/ITagRepository.kt#L22-L28](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/domain/src/main/kotlin/co/anitrend/domain/tag/repository/ITagRepository.kt#L22-L28)). - Data `TagRepository` (in `:data:tag`) implements `ITagRepository`, using a `TagSource` (which fetches from the AniList API and local DB) and returns a `DataState` flow (see [tag/repository/TagRepository.kt#L24-L31](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/data/src/main/kotlin/co/anitrend/data/tag/repository/TagRepository.kt#L24-L31)). - A Koin module in `:data:tag` binds `ITagRepository` to `TagRepository` and provides `TagUseCaseImpl` as the implementation of `TagUseCase` (often via a type alias or subclass) (see [genre/koin/Modules.kt#L99-L105](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/data/src/main/kotlin/co/anitrend/data/genre/koin/Modules.kt#L99-L105), [tag/usecase/TagUseCaseImpl.kt#L19-L25](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/data/src/main/kotlin/co/anitrend/data/tag/usecase/TagUseCaseImpl.kt#L19-L25)). - The UI (perhaps `TagViewModel` in a feature) gets a `TagUseCase` from Koin and calls `getMediaTags()`. The result is a flow (with loading and data) that the ViewModel can expose to the UI (Compose or fragment) to render a list of tags.

**Support-arch Integration:** The project uses the `support-arch` library (developed in-house) to standardize patterns: - **In Domain:** support-arch defines `UiState<T>` and related result wrappers for use case outputs, and possibly base use case classes. AniTrend’s domain use cases typically extend base classes from support-arch or follow its conventions (for example, some UseCases are parameterized by a `UiState` type). - **In Data:** support-arch provides abstract data source patterns. AniTrend data sources often extend `AbstractDataSource` from support-arch and use its provided mechanisms. The library’s `DataState<T>` class (a subtype of `UiState`) is heavily used to represent data streams with refresh/retry support (see [data/state/DataState.kt#L34-L42](https://github.com/AniTrend/support-arch/blob/1d33ef7ec3f48d4ba2bdeca82b55a23f0de0e2cc/data/src/main/kotlin/co/anitrend/arch/data/state/DataState.kt#L34-L42), [data/state/DataState.kt#L48-L56](https://github.com/AniTrend/support-arch/blob/1d33ef7ec3f48d4ba2bdeca82b55a23f0de0e2cc/data/src/main/kotlin/co/anitrend/arch/data/state/DataState.kt#L48-L56)). DataState pairs a Flow of the requested model with a Flow of loading states and handles common logic for refreshing or error retries. The data layer uses an idiom `source create source(params)` (using an infix function) to obtain a DataState from a data source (see [tag/repository/TagRepository.kt#L24-L31](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/data/src/main/kotlin/co/anitrend/data/tag/repository/TagRepository.kt#L24-L31)) – essentially wrapping a network/database call into a reactive stream with loading state. - **In Presentation:** support-arch provides base UI components and utilities. For example, `StateLayoutConfig` (from `arch.ui`) defines standard empty/loading/error visuals that the UI can use for a consistent look and feel. There are base fragment classes (e.g. `SupportFragment`, `SupportFragmentList`) and possibly base view model classes that handle common tasks. These can be extended to quickly create screens that conform to the app’s architecture (though with Jetpack Compose adoption, some of these base classes might be used less in favor of Compose patterns). - **Analytics & Logging:** support-arch has an `analytics` module which may integrate logging or analytics events, and an `extension` module with utility extensions. The project uses **Timber** for logging (added as a dependency globally), often via support-arch or directly.

## Jetpack Compose and UI Patterns

AniTrend v2 is largely built with **Jetpack Compose** for its UI, as indicated by the many Compose libraries and the Kotlin Compose plugin enabled in the build (see [plugins/components/ProjectPlugins.kt#L52-L58](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/buildSrc/src/main/java/co/anitrend/buildSrc/plugins/components/ProjectPlugins.kt#L52-L58)). Compose is used in feature modules for building screens and UI components. The app also uses **AndroidX Navigation Compose** for navigation between screens (rather than traditional Fragment navigation) (see [plugins/components/ProjectDependencies.kt#L392-L400](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/buildSrc/src/main/java/co/anitrend/buildSrc/plugins/components/ProjectDependencies.kt#L392-L400)).

However, the project likely mixes Compose with some existing View-based architecture components: - **ViewModels:** The app uses AndroidX Lifecycle ViewModel (and possibly Koin for injecting them). ViewModels manage `UiState`/`DataState` flows from the domain and convert them to Compose `State` or LiveData for UI. Compose integration is facilitated by libraries like `lifecycle-viewmodel-compose` and `compose.runtime.livedata` (see [plugins/components/ProjectDependencies.kt#L386-L395](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/buildSrc/src/main/java/co/anitrend/buildSrc/plugins/components/ProjectDependencies.kt#L386-L395), [plugins/components/ProjectDependencies.kt#L402-L410](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/buildSrc/src/main/java/co/anitrend/buildSrc/plugins/components/ProjectDependencies.kt#L402-L410)), which are included. - **Fragments/Activities:** There may still be a single Activity hosting the Compose navigation, or some fragments for specific features. The presence of `androidx.fragment` and support-arch fragment classes suggests some features might still use Fragments with Compose views or for dialog screens. The Navigation module (`:app:navigation`) likely sets up the NavHost and destinations for Compose screens. - The app uses **Material Design 3** components (Material3 Compose library) (see [gradle/libs.versions.toml#L8-L16](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/gradle/libs.versions.toml#L8-L16), [gradle/libs.versions.toml#L131-L139](https://github.com/AniTrend/anitrend-v2/blob/4931af9c33f9bb986507ef3a61a634aeed01550e/gradle/libs.versions.toml#L131-L139)) and theming from `support-arch:theme` for a consistent design. Themes and styles might be defined in common modules for reuse.

In summary, the architecture ensures: - Clear separation of concerns (UI vs data vs domain). - Reusability via modularization (common logic in shared modules, feature-specific code isolated). - Scalability for adding new features (just create new modules or extend existing ones with minimal impact on others). - Consistency via the support-arch framework (common patterns for loading states, error handling, etc. across the app).
